data.exact_reserve_text: The syndicate's approach to establishing the technical provision for claims outstanding and the reinsurers' share thereof has been similar to that at the previous year-end. Differences arose on the provisions established at the current year-end compared to the estimated ultimate costs of those claims at the previous year-end. The change amounts to an decrease in 2014 of previous provisions of GBP 18.0m (2013: GBP 0.5m decrease).

prior_year_events.impact_description: The 2012 year of account was materially impacted by Super storm Sandy in the last quarter of the 2012 calendar year.
Large loss activity in the Aviation division following the Tripoli Airport attack (Aviation war losses) impacted results.

named_events.loss_description: Materially impacted the 2012 year of account.
Aviation war losses including the Tripoli Airport attack affected the Aerospace division.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2014 were GBP 554.9m. The syndicate reports a prioryear movement in the provision for claims amounting to a net decrease of GBP 18.0m (a release), equivalent to about 3.24% of opening gross reserves. The release is described as favourable claims development, reflecting improving attritional experience in reunderwritten books (notably Property-related binder business). Offsetting items in the year included significant aviation war losses (Tripoli Airport attack) and strengthening in the General Liability book, but overall prior years produced a net release.
raw_causal_phrases: The change amounts to an decrease in 2014 of previous provisions of GBP 18.0m (2013: GBP 0.5m decrease).

We are pleased to report a profit for the 2012 closed year of account with a return on capacity of 7.1%, as previously reported the 2012 year of account was materially impacted by Super storm Sandy in the last quarter of the 2012 calendar year.

Following the decision in 2013 to change the underwriting strategy in the General Liability book the underwriting team left the Syndicate in 2014 and in the latter part of 2014 we recruited a new experienced team to take the account forward in a direction that will prove more profitable for the Syndicate. Given the increased loss experience in both this year and earlier years we have strengthened the reserving position on this account.

we continue to see the improvements in attritional loss experience in the books that were re-underwritten in recent years particularly the Property Division, both the Direct & Facultative and the North American Binder books.
large loss activity in the Energy division and during this calendar year Aviation war losses in particular the Tripoli Airport attack.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet 'Claims outstanding' prior-year column (2013) = GBP 554.9m. The only explicit prior-year movement found is stated as a net movement (note headed 'Change in the net provision for claims') describing a decrease of GBP 18.0m; no gross (insurance liabilities) prioryear movement column was provided, so the net figure has been used as a fallback per instructions. No gross claims development triangle was located in the provided pages. LOB-level reserve movements are inferred from narrative where stated (e.g. General Liability strengthening, Property attritional improvement) and are not quantified in the report.
